task: This is a synthetic writing exercise. Using these fictional reporting notes, write a newspaper news story for general readers. Draw only on the supplied notes; do not invent additional reported events, scenes, or quotations. Write from this reporting snapshot as of October 2, 2024. Include a headline. Target 450 to 650 words. Follow AP style.

facts.text: The National Transportation Safety Board released its final report on October 2, 2024, on the Millbrook Junction passenger train derailment of April 14, 2023.
The report concluded that a fatigue crack in a rail joint caused the derailment. The joint was four months overdue for its scheduled inspection.
The lead car left the rails at an estimated 73 miles per hour; the posted speed limit at the location was 79 mph.
Fourteen passengers sustained injuries, none life-threatening; the engineer and two conductors were uninjured.
The board determined that Consolidated Northern Railway last inspected the affected joint section in June 2021; the derailment occurred in April 2023.
CNR's track inspection manual calls for joint inspections at 18-month intervals; the 22-month gap exceeded that standard.
NTSB board member Rosa Mbeki, who led the investigation, said: "The crack was detectable with standard ultrasonic testing. It was not found because the test was not performed on schedule."
CNR spokesperson Dale Whitmore said the railroad accepted the findings and had already completed a system-wide inspection of all joints in the affected track class.
The board issued five safety recommendations, including mandatory electronic logging of inspection dates accessible to federal rail safety inspectors in real time.
Investigators found the engineer had not exceeded authorized speed but that speed contributed to the severity of derailment once the rail failed.
CNR's safety records showed 11 missed or delayed joint inspections on the route between 2019 and 2023; the Millbrook Junction joint was the only one that showed a crack.
The railroad has since installed continuous rail monitoring sensors on 340 kilometers of track on the same route.
Passenger rail injuries from track-related causes averaged 31 per year nationally in the five years before the Millbrook derailment.
The injured passengers reached a settlement with CNR in December 2023; financial terms were not disclosed.
Federal rail safety inspectors audited CNR's track inspection program in 2021 and found it compliant at the time.
Millbrook Junction is a mid-speed corridor with an authorized maximum of 79 mph over most of its length.
The fatigue crack measured 4.7 centimeters at its widest point when recovered from the wreckage.
CNR operates 9,200 route-kilometers of track across 11 states.
The April 2023 derailment was CNR's first involving passenger injuries since a 2017 station collision that injured two people.

forbidden_additions: a claim that CNR knew of the crack before the derailment
a fine or criminal charge against CNR or its employees
